Currently, the project has garnered over 43,000 stars and 9,000 forks on GitHub.

title: MG1937/ASC
content: ASC is a super FAST Android decompiler front-end designed for Agents/Mobile Researchers. - MG1937/ASC When decompiling massive Android APKs, the standard procedure is to wait. We wait for tools to eat gigabytes of RAM, fully inflate the artifacts, and spend tens of minutes building heavy global indexes and cross references... All of this is just to guarantee fast code searches later, but here is the contradiction. A compiled artifact is already highly structured, modern decompilers never utilize this, they waste massive amounts of time and memory reconstructing a bloated database of code relationships over already structured data. This engineering approach defies common sense. When I can directly extract any code relationship from the APK in milliseconds, does this preprocessing still hold any value? Instead of forcing decompilers into heavy preprocessing, we choose to query the compiled artifact directly as a database. We built a stateless, zero-overhead engine that extracts and searches code on demand in milliseconds. In this briefing, we will explore the underlying engineering required to bypass traditional bottlenecks. We will demonstrate how to abandon full inflate by probing directly within the Deflate bitstream, building dense Huffman lookup tables to extract core metadata without touching irrelevant data blocks. title: Nail the Narrative
content: content Videos Content Index Fragments Board Games Photography Thoughtworks Home Insights Careers Radar Engineering follow RSS Mastodon LinkedIn Bluesky X BGG Top Narrative first, visuals next What are you saying and to whom? Building the storyline Collaborative whiteboarding Diagram-centric narratives Narrative-based writing Voice memos + AI Create a storyboard to make your plan concrete Storyboarding using slides Sidebars Do our points of view have to be “unique”? Try it yourself Nail your narrative Before opening any slide software, nail your narrative. Start by distilling your big idea — your unique point of view and what’s at stake — and build an audience persona so you know who you’re speaking to. Then flesh out a storyline using a structure that fits your content, whether through whiteboarding, writing, or voice memos and AI. Finally, turn that narrative into a lightweight storyboard, so your slide design work becomes an exercise in execution rather than invention. 15 September 2026 Sumeet Gayathri Moghe Sumeet is the global head of culture and organisational design at Thoughtworks. In his past life, he was a software technologist for over two decades, working as a business analyst, product manager and transformation consultant.
